purposes.openai: Fetch generated logo image from OpenAI image blob storage

summary: alanagoyal/branded uses supabase through @supabase/ssr 0.12.7 in 46 places; supabase through @supabase/supabase-js 2.114.0 in 9 places; stripe through stripe 15.12.0 in 8 places; braintrust through braintrust 3.34.0 in 6 places; openai for Chat completions via Braintrust proxy (baseURL braintrustproxy.com/v1) through openai 4.104.0, pinned to gpt-4o-mini in 4 places; whoxy for WHOIS domain availability through raw HTTP in 2 places; stripe through webhooks in 1 place; vercel through @vercel/analytics 1.6.1 in 1 place; rapidapi-uspto-trademark for USPTO trademark search via RapidAPI through raw HTTP, pinned to /v1/ in 1 place; npm-registry for npm package name availability through raw HTTP in 1 place; openai for Fetch generated logo image from OpenAI image blob storage through raw HTTP in 1 place.
agentSummary:
I found and recorded five more usages, on top of the ones the scan had already recorded. I did not read the call sites the scan recorded earlier for Supabase, Stripe, Braintrust, the OpenAI logo call and Vercel Analytics. I also did not read the repo's scripts or CI files for other network calls.

**Recorded this pass:**
- **Whoxy** (`api.whoxy.com`, raw HTTP): WHOIS lookups for domain availability. It is called from `app/find-domain-availability/route.ts` and `app/generate-names/route.ts`. The key comes from `WHOXY_API_KEY`.
- **RapidAPI USPTO trademark search** (`uspto-trademark.p.rapidapi.com`, raw HTTP): called from `app/find-trademarks/route.ts`. It pins `/v1/` in the path, and the key comes from `RAPID_API_KEY`.
- **npm registry** (`registry.npmjs.org`, raw HTTP): `app/find-npm-availability/route.ts` treats a 404 as "name available".
- **OpenAI chat completions through the Braintrust proxy** (SDK): three routes (`find-npm-names`, `generate-names`, `generate-one-pager-content`) point the OpenAI client at `braintrustproxy.com/v1`. They use model `gpt-4o-mini`. I recorded the calls under the existing `openai` SDK usage and added the proxy host as a hint.
- **OpenAI image blob storage** (`oaidalleapiprodscus.blob.core.windows.net`, raw HTTP): `lib/one-pager-logo.ts` downloads the generated logo before it goes into the PDF. It only accepts that host and disables redirects.

**Leads that are not external APIs:**
- **Own-backend fetches:** The `fetch` calls in `components/names-display.tsx` (lines 286, 354, 428), `command-menu.tsx`, `user-nav.tsx` and `verify-subscription.tsx` go to the repo's own routes. So do `account-form`, `checkout`, `delete-account`, `name-generator`, `pricing` and `share`.
- **Client-side libraries:** The Radix, UI, form, `zod`, `react`, `next` and `uuid` dependencies make no network calls. The same goes for `@react-pdf/renderer`.
- **Links and test fixtures:** The Namecheap affiliate link, the USPTO TSDR link, `docs.npmjs.com`, the company logo links, `branded.ai`, and the test hosts (`evil.example`, `attacker.example` and similar) are links or fixtures, not API calls.
- **Env names:** `NEXT_PUBLIC_ALPHARUN_URL` is a link in the UI.

**Unsure or not read:**
- `npm-name` is a dependency, but I didn't check whether anything imports it.
- `@stripe/stripe-js` and `@vercel/og` are declared in `package.json`, but I found no code that uses them.
- `scripts/test-pdf-runtime.cjs:77` calls the app's own `/one-pager` route, so I did not record it.
- I did not check the Stripe call sites in `lib/billing.ts`, `portal-session` and `update-subscription` (the scan found no call there).
- Several routes call `requireUser` and `reserveUsage` from `lib/provider-access.ts`. Their Supabase calls were already recorded.
